skill.name: ultracave
skill.description: Compresses assistant responses into terse fragments while preserving technical substance, code, commands, paths, errors, numbers, units, and negations. Invoke with /ultracave or /caveman ultra, and stop with "stop caveman" or "normal mode".
skill.summary: A persistent terse-response mode that removes filler while preserving essential technical details.
skill.author: juliusbrussee

content.value_statement: Long assistant replies slow readers and hide the facts that matter. Ultracave produces compact fragments while preserving technical substance and safety-critical details.
actual_capabilities: Rewrites responses as concise fragments with reduced grammar.
Preserves code, commands, paths, API names, error strings, numbers, and units.
Avoids repeated facts and removes unnecessary filler.
Maintains an active mode across the session until a supported stop phrase.
Uses plain prose for security warnings, irreversible actions, and ambiguous statements.
limitations: It changes response style, not the assistant model or its factual accuracy.
It does not guarantee shorter output when code, commands, or required details must remain.
It depends on the host tool recognizing the slash command or skill invocation.
It is unsuitable for onboarding, security reviews, and text intended for broad audiences.

use_cases.title: Scan Technical Answers Faster
use_cases.description: Reduce filler in coding answers while keeping commands, paths, errors, and implementation details visible.

use_cases.title: Keep Incident Notes Compact
use_cases.description: Capture operational facts and next actions in short, scannable responses during fast-moving support work.

use_cases.title: Review Dense Conversations
use_cases.description: Use compact summaries and direct fragments when reading many assistant responses or managing limited context.

prompt_templates.title: Start Compact Mode
prompt_templates.prompt: /ultracave. Explain this task in terse fragments while preserving all technical details.

prompt_templates.title: Compress an Explanation
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite the explanation below in Ultracave style. Keep code, commands, paths, numbers, units, and negations unchanged: [paste explanation].

prompt_templates.title: Keep Facts Once
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Ultracave mode. Turn this implementation plan into a non-repeating checklist. Preserve ordering, dependencies, commands, and failure conditions: [paste plan].
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert a detailed plan into an efficient work list

prompt_templates.title: Handle a Risky Action
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Ultracave mode for the response, but explain the security warning in plain prose and request confirmation before any irreversible action: [describe action].

output_examples.input: Explain why an inline object prop can cause extra React renders.
output_examples.output: Inline object prop, new reference each render, re-render. Use useMemo.

output_examples.input: Give the database migration order when a column will be removed.
What should happen before an irreversible production action?
output_examples.output: Plain warning. Explain impact. Confirm first.

best_practices: Invoke the mode only when the audience can interpret fragments.
Keep technical tokens, negations, numbers, and units verbatim.
Use explicit stop phrases before switching back to normal responses.
anti_patterns: Do not use compressed fragments for onboarding or public documentation.
Do not remove warnings, conditions, or confirmation requests to save words.
Do not assume shorter output means more accurate output.

faq.question: How do I activate Ultracave?
faq.answer: Use /ultracave or /caveman ultra when the host tool supports the skill.

faq.question: What does Ultracave preserve?
faq.answer: It preserves code, commands, paths, API names, error strings, numbers, units, and negations.

faq.question: Does Ultracave run commands?
faq.answer: No. It changes response style and does not provide command execution.

faq.question: Will every response be a fragment?
faq.answer: No. It uses plain prose for warnings, irreversible actions, ambiguity, and user confusion.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Developers and technical readers who prefer fast, compact responses. It is not intended for onboarding or public-facing prose.
